root_cause: Authorization is enforced almost entirely by route middleware, not by controllers or policies. There are only 2 Policy classes against 81 controllers, so the middleware list is the single point of control. Any verb or resource that is not explicitly listed is unprotected.
correct_behaviour_preserved: super-admin bypass lives in PermissionMiddleware::handle() and is intentionally absent from RolePermissionChecker - a documented, test-pinned asymmetry that must not be 'fixed'.
Permission resolution is by role slug via Role::grantedPermissions(), cached 3600s under role_permissions:{slug}, compared with strict in_array.
A missing role resolves to an empty permission list, not an error.
recommended_remediation_order: 1. SEC-03 PUT /api/roles/{role}/permissions - smallest change, largest impact (privilege escalation).
2. SEC-01 PATCH bookings - restrict the verb or narrow the validated fields.
3. SEC-02 /api/v2/* - decide per route whether it is intentionally public (coverage/availability/recommendations look intentional) or a leak (finance, booking writes).
blocked: All of the above change authorization outcomes, so none were applied in Phase 0.16.
